title: Topic Drill: Revising Essays: Organization, Transitions, Cohesion and Style (Set A)

items.stem:
(1) The campus career fair will fill the gym on Thursday from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. (2) More than forty employers have registered, and each will bring recruiters from several departments. (3) The gym floor was refinished last summer with a new coat of gloss. (4) Students should bring printed resumes and plan which tables to visit first.

Which sentence should be deleted to improve the unity of this announcement?
options: Sentence 2, because the number of employers is not relevant to students.
Sentence 1, because the time and place of an event do not belong in an announcement.
Sentence 4, because advice for students repeats the purpose of the announcement.
Sentence 3, because the floor refinishing does not help students prepare for the fair.
items.explanation: The announcement is about attending and preparing for the fair, so the detail about the refinished gym floor wanders off topic. The number of employers, the schedule, and the advice about resumes all help a student decide how to take part, so removing any of them would weaken the notice.

items.stem:
______ Each Tuesday and Thursday, volunteers meet with second graders for thirty minutes of reading practice. They choose picture books together, take turns reading aloud, and talk about the story afterward. Teachers report that several children now ask to read at home.

Which sentence would be the best topic sentence for this paragraph?
options: The volunteer tutoring program has helped young students build confidence in reading.
Reading is an important skill that everyone needs throughout life.
Volunteers must complete a short training session before they begin tutoring.
Picture books are available in many colors, sizes, and subjects.
items.explanation: A good topic sentence names the paragraph’s main idea: what the tutoring program does and the result described. The general statement about reading is too broad to introduce these particulars. Training is a detail the paragraph never discusses. Picture books appear only as one small detail, so that choice is too narrow.

items.stem:
(1) The city’s composting pilot collected food scraps from 200 Eastside homes through the spring. (2) Pickups ran on time almost every week. (3) ______, many residents said the program was hard to follow. (4) The instructions arrived late, and the list of accepted items kept changing.

Which transition best fills the blank at the start of sentence 3?
options: For example
Even so
As a result
Likewise
items.explanation: Sentence 2 reports something positive, and sentence 3 reports a problem, so the two ideas contrast. Even so signals that contrast. For example would promise an illustration of smooth pickups. As a result would claim the on time pickups caused the confusion. Likewise would suggest the two sentences say similar things, which they do not.

items.stem:
(1) The student council surveyed 300 students about school lunch. (2) The survey asked about portion size, taste, and cost. (3) Most students wanted larger portions. (4) Most students also wanted more fresh fruit.

Which is the best way to combine sentences 3 and 4?
options: Most students wanted larger portions, most students also wanted more fresh fruit.
Most students wanted larger portions, because most students also wanted more fresh fruit.
Most students wanted larger portions and more fresh fruit.
Most students wanted larger portions and also most students wanted more fresh fruit as well.
items.explanation: Both sentences share a subject and verb, so the two requests can be joined as a compound object with and, which removes the repetition. The second choice is a comma splice. Because falsely makes the fruit request the cause of the portion request. The last choice stays wordy, repeating most students and adding also and as well together.

items.stem:
(1) Every first Saturday, neighbors on Maple Court bring unused tools to the community garage. (2) A borrowed drill or ladder can save a family the cost of buying one for a single job. (3) People also meet neighbors they might never have spoken to otherwise. (4) The swap has grown from six households to more than thirty.

Which sentence would be the best concluding sentence for this paragraph?
options: By sharing what they already own, the neighbors save money and strengthen their community.
Tools are made of metal, wood, and plastic.
Next month’s swap will be held in the garage at 9 a.m.
Some people think that sharing tools is not always a good idea, because tools can get lost or worn out.
items.explanation: A strong conclusion pulls together the paragraph’s two benefits, savings and friendship. The sentence about materials adds an unrelated fact. The announcement of next month’s time is a new detail, not a summary. The sentence about doubts about sharing introduces an idea the paragraph never develops and cuts against its point.

items.stem:
Our science club learned that a weather balloon launch depends on careful preparation. Before launch day, we checked the wind forecast so the balloon would not drift over the highway. ______ By the time the balloon rose, every job had an owner.

Which detail best supports the claim that the club prepared carefully?
options: The balloon was white and about as tall as a door.
Several members said they were excited to watch the balloon rise.
Weather balloons have been used by scientists for many decades, and they remain a common way to study the upper air.
Each member was assigned a task, such as filling the balloon, tracking the radio signal, or recording the time.
items.explanation: The claim is about preparation, and giving every member a defined task is a concrete example of it. The balloon’s color and size describe appearance, not planning. Excitement is a feeling, not evidence of preparation. The history of weather balloons is true but does not show what this club did.

items.stem:
To: All Staff

(1) Hey everybody, the copier on the second floor is totally dead again. (2) Please use the one near the front desk until it gets fixed. (3) A repair technician is scheduled for Friday.

Which revision of sentence 1 best fits the formal tone of a workplace memo?
options: Hey all, the second floor copier is toast, and I am so over it.
The copier on the second floor has gone kaput, which is a big bummer.
The copier on the second floor is out of service again.
It is with great regret that this writer must inform each and every employee that the copier is not functioning properly.
items.explanation: The correct revision removes the casual greeting and slang while staying brief and clear. The first wrong choice keeps slang and a personal complaint. The second uses informal words such as kaput and bummer. The last overshoots into stiff, wordy language, which is not the plain professional tone a memo needs.

items.stem:
The bookbinding workshop meets on Wednesday evenings at the community center. (1) At the present time, the workshop is in the process of accepting new members who wish to join. (2) Participants learn to sew signatures and attach covers. (3) All materials are provided.

Which revision of sentence 1 is the most concise without losing meaning?
options: At this point in time, the workshop is currently accepting new members who want to join.
The workshop is now accepting new members.
Currently the workshop is in the process of accepting members who are new.
The workshop accepts new members, and it is accepting them now at present.
items.explanation: Phrases such as at the present time and in the process of add words without adding meaning, and wish to join repeats what accepting new members already says. The correct choice keeps the full meaning in seven words. Each wrong choice keeps redundant time words or repeats the idea of accepting members.

items.stem:
(1) Finally, the city will decide whether to buy more buses based on the results. (2) The electric bus trial began in September on Route 12. (3) Drivers recorded charging times and battery use for each trip. (4) After ten weeks, riders were asked to complete a short survey.

Which order of sentences is the most logical for this paragraph?
options: Sentence 2, sentence 4, sentence 3, sentence 1
Sentence 3, sentence 2, sentence 4, sentence 1
Sentence 1, sentence 2, sentence 3, sentence 4
Sentence 2, sentence 3, sentence 4, sentence 1
items.explanation: The paragraph should open with how the trial began, move through the data drivers gathered, then the rider survey after ten weeks, and end with the final decision signaled by Finally. Putting the survey before the driver data breaks the sequence of the trial. Starting with the data skips the introduction. Putting the decision first removes its meaning.

items.stem:
(1) Last year, many students came to the career fair without a plan. (2) They waited in long lines at a few popular tables and missed several others. (3) ______, the career center will post the employer list online a week early.

Which transition best fills the blank at the start of sentence 3?
options: To prevent this problem
Similarly, in the same way as last year
In addition
For example
items.explanation: Sentence 3 describes a step taken in response to the trouble in sentences 1 and 2, so a phrase of purpose fits. Similarly would link two parallel ideas. In addition would add an unrelated point. For example would suggest the early list is an instance of the long lines, which it is not.

items.stem:
(1) The composting pilot ended in June with good results. (2) Residents kept 18 tons of food scraps out of the landfill. (3) The pilot began in January with 200 homes. (4) City staff now plan to expand it to 600 homes next year.

Which sentence should be moved to the beginning of the paragraph so the ideas follow time order?
options: Sentence 4, so the paragraph starts with the plan for next year.
Sentence 2, so the paragraph starts with the total amount of scraps.
Sentence 3, so the paragraph starts with how the pilot began.
Sentence 1, so the paragraph starts with the ending of the pilot.
items.explanation: Time order requires the start of the pilot to come first, then its end and results, then future plans. Sentence 3 gives the January start, so it belongs at the front. Opening with next year’s plan, the final tonnage, or the June ending would place later events before earlier ones and confuse the sequence.

items.stem:
(1) The tutors arrive at four o’clock. (2) The tutors set up the tables. (3) The tutors lay out the books. (4) The tutors greet the children at the door.

Which revision best improves the sentence variety in this paragraph?
options: The tutors arrive at four o’clock. They set up the tables. They lay out the books. They greet the children at the door.
When the tutors arrive at four o’clock, they set up the tables, lay out the books, and greet the children at the door.
The tutors arrive at four o’clock and the tutors set up the tables and the tutors lay out the books and the tutors greet the children.
Arriving at four o’clock, the children are greeted at the door by tutors who set up the tables and lay out the books.
items.explanation: The correct choice opens with a subordinate clause and joins the three actions in a series, which removes the repeated short pattern. Swapping the subject for they leaves four choppy sentences. The run of and links is repetitive and unclear. The last choice has a dangling modifier, since the children did not arrive at four to set up tables.

items.stem:
Dear Principal Reyes:

(1) The student council surveyed 300 students about the cafeteria menu. (2) Lots of kids said the food is totally gross. (3) We would like to meet with you to discuss the results.

Which revision of sentence 2 best fits the purpose and audience of this letter?
options: Everybody hates the food, so something has to change right now.
The menu, in our considered opinion, is characterized by deficiencies of a most unfortunate nature.
Some students said the cafeteria closes too early for them to eat.
Many students described the menu as unappetizing, and several named the cooked vegetables as the main problem.
items.explanation: A respectful letter to a principal needs a polite, specific tone that reports the survey findings. The correct choice does that. The first wrong choice is exaggerated and demanding. The second is inflated and vague. The last is polite but shifts to a different complaint, closing time, that the survey of the menu did not address.

items.stem:
______ Riders on Route 12 noticed the quiet engine and the smooth start. Drivers said the buses climbed Alder Street hill without strain. Even so, the buses needed charging every night, which limited evening service.

Which sentence would be the best topic sentence for this paragraph?
options: Buses have carried passengers in cities for more than a hundred years.
The city bought three buses for the trial and chose Route 12 because it is busy all day.
The electric buses earned mostly positive reactions during the trial, with one clear limit.
Alder Street hill is one of the steepest streets in the city.
items.explanation: The paragraph reports praise from riders and drivers and then one drawback, and only the correct choice covers both parts. The history of buses is too broad. The purchase is a detail the paragraph does not discuss. The hill is mentioned only as one example of performance, so a topic sentence about its steepness is far too narrow.

items.stem:
(1) Our balloon reached about 30,000 meters before it burst. (2) The camera on board recorded the curve of the horizon and a sky that turned from blue to deep violet. (3) A parachute carried the payload down to a field twelve kilometers from the launch site. (4) We found it the next morning.

Which sentence would be the best concluding sentence for this account of the launch?
options: The camera on board was a small, inexpensive model.
The launch showed our club that careful planning and teamwork can carry a small experiment surprisingly far.
Many other clubs in the region also launch weather balloons and share their results every year.
Next, I will describe how the balloon was made.
items.explanation: A concluding sentence should reflect on the whole account. The correct choice ties the high flight and the safe recovery to a lesson. The camera detail adds a new minor fact. Mentioning other clubs shifts focus away from this launch. Announcing the next topic points forward instead of closing out the account.

items.stem:
The bookbinding workshop has a waiting list this season. (1) Marisol folded the paper into small bundles. (2) She sewed each bundle to the spine with waxed thread. (3) Then she glued the cover boards in place.

Which is the best way to combine sentences 1 and 2 to show the order of the steps?
options: After Marisol folded the paper into small bundles, she sewed each bundle to the spine with waxed thread.
Marisol folded the paper into small bundles, she sewed each bundle to the spine with waxed thread.
Marisol folded the paper into small bundles, so she sewed each bundle to the spine with waxed thread.
Marisol folded the paper into small bundles while sewing each bundle to the spine with waxed thread.
items.explanation: After shows that folding came first and sewing came second, which matches the steps. The first wrong choice is a comma splice. So claims that folding caused the sewing, a cause and effect link the steps do not have. While suggests she did both at once, which is impossible, and it also creates an awkward fragment of action.

items.stem:
(1) The student council needs your help with the lunch survey. (2) Every homeroom will receive ten paper forms on Monday. (3) The cafeteria’s walls were painted bright yellow over the summer. (4) Please return the completed forms to the front office by Friday.

Which sentence is least related to the main point of this notice and should be removed?
options: Sentence 2, because the number of forms is not needed by students.
Sentence 3, because the paint color has nothing to do with completing the survey.
Sentence 4, because the return date is already clear from sentence 1.
Sentence 1, because the council’s request should come after the instructions.
items.explanation: The notice explains how to take part in the survey, so details about the forms and the deadline are useful. The wall color is the only sentence that does not help a student complete or return a form. Sentence 1 states the purpose and works well as an opener, and sentence 4 adds a deadline that sentence 1 lacks.

items.stem:
(1) Next, the volunteers matched each reader with a book at the right level. (2) First, the program coordinator sorted the incoming students by grade. (3) In the final step, tutors wrote a short note about each student’s progress. (4) Then pairs sat together for thirty minutes of reading.

Which order of sentences makes this description of a tutoring session the most logical?
options: Sentence 2, sentence 1, sentence 4, sentence 3
Sentence 2, sentence 4, sentence 1, sentence 3
Sentence 1, sentence 2, sentence 3, sentence 4
Sentence 4, sentence 2, sentence 1, sentence 3
items.explanation: The signal words give the order: first the coordinator sorts students, next volunteers match readers with books, then pairs read together, and in the final step tutors write notes. Reading before matching a book would not make sense. Starting with Next or with the reading sentence ignores the signal words First and Next.

items.stem:
Our neighborhood tool swap is more than a way to save money. Neighbors who borrow a ladder or a saw also learn each other’s names. ______ One retired carpenter now teaches a monthly class on sharpening blades, and the garage fills with people who were strangers a year ago.

Which detail best supports the claim that the swap builds community?
options: The swap holds more than two hundred tools.
Hammers and wrenches are the most borrowed items.
Teens and older neighbors now work side by side on repair days.
The garage is open on the first Saturday of every month and has plenty of parking.
items.explanation: The claim is about relationships, so the best support shows people from different groups working together. The number of tools, the most borrowed items, and the schedule are accurate details about the swap itself, but none of them shows neighbors connecting with one another, so none supports the claim about community.

items.stem:
(1) Volunteers at the tutoring program work with students on reading and math. (2) Last year, about sixty students joined. (3) Students who attended all year improved their grades. ______ the program now wants to add a second weekly session.

Which transition best fills the blank to begin the final sentence?
options: On the other hand,
In the same way,
Before long,
Because of these gains,
items.explanation: The final sentence names a decision that follows from the improved grades, so a cause and effect transition fits. On the other hand signals a contrast the passage does not contain. In the same way suggests a comparison with something else. Before long refers to the passing of time rather than to a reason.

items.stem:
Subject: Career Fair Volunteers

(1) Dear Ms. Okafor, (2) I am writing to ask whether the business club could help check in employers at the career fair. (3) We figured you guys probably need extra hands since it’s gonna be packed. (4) Our members can arrive at eight o’clock on Thursday.

Which revision of sentence 3 best maintains the formal tone of this email to a staff member?
options: We figured you guys probably need extra hands since it’s gonna be packed.
We know you will certainly be thrilled to accept our totally awesome offer.
We believe extra help may be useful because a large crowd is expected.
Since a large crowd is expected, the business club most respectfully and humbly begs for the chance to assist.
items.explanation: The email is addressed to a staff member, so it needs polite, standard language. The correct choice gives a clear reason in a formal tone. The original uses slang and contractions such as gonna. The second assumes the reader will be thrilled and uses casual wording. The last is overdone and pleading, which sounds unnatural.

items.stem:
WANTED: Bookbinders of Every Level

(1) Have you ever wanted to make a book with your own hands? (2) The Saturday workshop teaches sewing, folding, and covering, and it welcomes complete beginners. (3) A parent of one student wrote a formal statement of the institutional benefits of the program.

The workshop is preparing this flyer for teenagers. Which revision of sentence 3 best fits the purpose and audience?
options: Come make a notebook you can take home, and bring a friend along.
Prospective participants are advised to review the enclosed policy regarding enrollment and fees.
The workshop was discussed at a recent meeting, and several members gave opinions.
A notebook is a bound set of pages that may be used for writing.
items.explanation: A flyer for teenagers should be inviting, direct, and brief, and the correct choice speaks to the reader and names a clear reward. The enrollment line is stiff and bureaucratic. The meeting line is about the organization, not the reader. The definition explains something the audience already knows and makes no invitation.

items.stem:
______ In the pilot, residents sorted scraps into one small bin and set it out each Monday. Most families said the routine took less than two minutes a day. Several also said their kitchen trash smelled better.

Which sentence would be the best topic sentence for this paragraph?
options: Composting is a topic of growing interest in many parts of the world.
Participants found the composting routine quick and easy to follow.
Food scraps include peels, coffee grounds, and eggshells.
The city spent a large part of its yearly budget on trash pickup.
items.explanation: The paragraph shows how simple the routine was, from one bin to two minutes a day, and the correct choice states that main idea. The first wrong choice is too broad to focus the paragraph. The list of scraps is a minor detail. The budget claim moves to an unrelated idea about city spending.

items.stem:
(1) The tool swap began with a table of tools in Dev’s driveway. (2) The swap soon outgrew the driveway. (3) The swap moved to the garage on Maple Court. (4) The swap now attracts thirty households.

Which revision best improves the cohesion and flow of these sentences?
options: The tool swap began with a table of tools in Dev’s driveway. The swap soon outgrew the driveway. The swap moved to the garage on Maple Court. The swap now attracts thirty households.
Beginning in Dev’s driveway, thirty households now attract the tool swap in the garage on Maple Court.
The tool swap began in Dev’s driveway, and moved to the garage on Maple Court, it now attracts thirty households.
The tool swap began with a table of tools in Dev’s driveway, but it soon outgrew that space and moved to the garage on Maple Court, where it now attracts thirty households.
items.explanation: The correct choice links the events in time order and replaces the repeated subject with pronouns and connecting words. The first wrong choice keeps the repetition. The second has a dangling modifier and reverses who attracts whom. The third has a misplaced comma and a run on that joins two clauses without a proper connection.

items.stem:
(1) The electric bus on Route 12 reduced noise along Alder Street. (2) It cut fuel costs by about a third compared to a diesel bus on the same route. (3) The city reported fewer complaints about exhaust smells at the downtown stops. (4) Riders also said the ride felt smoother on the hill.

Which sentence would be the best concluding sentence for this paragraph?
options: The bus was painted green and white, like the city’s other buses.
Riders on other routes may have different opinions about electric buses, and more data would be needed before anyone could say.
Taken together, these results suggest that electric buses can improve both the cost and the comfort of city service.
Diesel buses will probably never be used in any city again.
items.explanation: A fitting conclusion sums up the reported benefits, noise, cost, smell, and ride, in one general statement. The paint color is a trivial detail. The sentence about other routes introduces speculation that the paragraph does not explore. The last choice overstates the evidence with an extreme prediction the facts cannot support.

items.stem:
(1) The weather balloon carried a small radio. (2) The radio sent its position to our laptop every ten seconds. (3) The laptop displayed the balloon’s path on a map.

Which is the best way to combine sentences 1 and 2?
options: The weather balloon carried a small radio, the radio sent its position to our laptop every ten seconds.
The weather balloon carried a small radio that sent its position to our laptop every ten seconds.
The weather balloon carried a small radio, but the radio sent its position to our laptop every ten seconds.
The weather balloon carried a small radio and then it was sending its position, which was every ten seconds, to our laptop.
items.explanation: Sentence 2 describes the radio, so a relative clause beginning with that joins them smoothly. The first wrong choice is a comma splice. But wrongly signals a contrast between carrying a radio and sending signals. The last choice is wordy and shifts tense and structure, which confuses the connection between the two ideas.

items.stem:
(1) Binding a book by hand takes patience, but the steps are easy to learn. (2) First, participants fold sheets of paper in half to make signatures. (3) Next, they stack the signatures and sew them together. (4) The workshop owns a small hand press that was donated years ago. (5) Finally, they glue on a cover.

Which sentence should be moved or removed to keep this paragraph focused on the steps of binding a book?
options: Sentence 1 should be moved to the end, because it is a conclusion.
Sentence 3 should be removed, because sewing is a part of the process that readers already know.
Sentence 5 should be moved to the beginning, because the cover is the most important part.
Sentence 4 should be removed, because the press is not one of the steps.
items.explanation: The paragraph lists the steps in order with signal words, and the sentence about the donated press interrupts that sequence without being a step. Sentence 1 works as an opening idea. Sentence 3 is a necessary step. Moving sentence 5 would put the final step first and destroy the order.

items.stem:
(1) Next, we attached the camera and a small parachute to the payload box. (2) Once the seams were sound, we filled the balloon with helium until it was about two meters wide. (3) At last, we released the balloon and watched it climb above the trees. (4) To begin, we checked every seam for leaks.

Which order of sentences makes this account the most logical?
options: Sentence 4, sentence 2, sentence 1, sentence 3
Sentence 2, sentence 4, sentence 1, sentence 3
Sentence 4, sentence 1, sentence 2, sentence 3
Sentence 2, sentence 1, sentence 3, sentence 4
items.explanation: To begin marks the seam check as the first step, and Once the seams were sound shows that filling comes next. Attaching the camera follows, and At last marks the release as the final step. Putting the seam check after filling, or after the release, makes no sense because leaks must be found first.

items.stem:
Riders gave the electric bus trial high marks for comfort. ______ Maya Ortiz, who rides Route 12 to work, said the bus was so quiet that she could read the whole way. Another rider said he no longer arrived with a headache from engine noise.

Which detail best supports the claim that riders found the buses comfortable?
options: The trial ran for ten weeks beginning in September.
In the survey, 84 percent of riders rated the ride smoother than on older buses.
Route 12 passes through the center of the city and stops near several schools and shops.
The city plans to discuss the trial at its next meeting.
items.explanation: The claim concerns comfort, so a survey result about a smoother ride directly backs it up. The length of the trial, the path of the route, and the plan for a meeting are all accurate facts about the trial, but none of them says anything about how comfortable the riders felt.

items.stem:
To: Facilities Staff

(1) In the event that a leak is discovered, employees are required to make an immediate report of it. (2) The report should be made to the front desk. (3) A mop and bucket are kept in the closet by the lobby.

Which revision of sentence 1 is the most concise while keeping a formal tone?
options: Employees should report any leak immediately.
If a leak is discovered, then it is required that an immediate report be made by employees.
Report any leaks right away, okay?
In the event that a leak should be found, employees must make a report of the leak without delay.
items.explanation: The correct choice states the same requirement in six words and keeps a professional voice. The first wrong choice uses a passive, wordy construction. The second is brief but casual. The last is formal but wordy, repeating leak and using several empty phrases such as in the event that and make a report of.

items.stem:
The balloon launch went well. (1) We tracked it for two hours. (2) ______, the signal faded when the balloon passed behind a ridge. (3) We drove toward its last known position and found it in a field.

Which transition best fills the blank at the start of sentence 2?
options: Therefore
Instead
For instance
Eventually
items.explanation: Sentence 2 reports an event that happened later in time, after two hours of tracking, so a time transition fits. Therefore would claim that tracking caused the fading signal. Instead would suggest a replacement of one action by another. For instance would introduce an example of the tracking, which the fading signal is not.

items.stem:
______ Neighbors can borrow a ladder for a day, a sander for a weekend, or a tile cutter for a single project. Each tool carries a tag with the owner’s name and the date it is due back. Most items return on time, and a small notebook records any repairs.

Which sentence would be the best topic sentence for this paragraph?
options: Many people enjoy fixing things around their homes.
Tags are small pieces of paper or card with names and dates written on them.
The tool swap runs on a simple system of borrowing and returning.
Every neighborhood in the city should have its own tool swap.
items.explanation: The paragraph describes how borrowing, tags, due dates, and a repair notebook work, so a topic sentence about the system covers it. The first wrong choice is broad and drifts from this swap. The tag definition is too narrow. The last choice makes a recommendation that the paragraph never argues.

items.stem:
(1) The city’s composting pilot started in January. (2) The pilot reached 200 homes. (3) The pilot lasted six months. (4) The pilot kept 18 tons of food out of the landfill. (5) The pilot was popular with residents.

Which revision best improves the sentence variety of this paragraph?
options: Starting in January, the city’s composting pilot reached 200 homes and, over six months, kept 18 tons of food out of the landfill, which pleased residents.
The city’s composting pilot started in January. It reached 200 homes. It lasted six months. It kept 18 tons of food out of the landfill. It was popular.
The city’s composting pilot started in January and it reached 200 homes and it lasted six months and it kept 18 tons out of the landfill.
Starting in January, residents were pleased by 200 homes reached by the six months of the city’s pilot, with 18 tons kept out.
items.explanation: The correct choice varies the sentence openings and joins related facts with a participial phrase and a clear connecting clause. Replacing the subject with it keeps five short, similar sentences. The string of and links runs on without variety. The last choice scrambles the relationships, and the modifiers no longer attach to the right subjects.

items.stem:
Hi Mr. Delgado,

(1) The career fair is on Thursday. (2) My business club would like to help set up the tables. (3) I am writing to ask for permission, since the gym is reserved through your office.

This email is written to a school staff member. Which revision of sentence 1 best fits the purpose and audience?
options: Thursday is the career fair, so we are gonna help set up.
I am writing to ask whether our club may help set up the tables for the career fair on Thursday.
The career fair is occurring on Thursday as part of the regular schedule of the institution.
We want to help, and we are sure you will agree that this is the best plan.
items.explanation: The correct choice states a clear request politely, which fits an email to a staff member asking for permission. The first wrong choice is casual and does not ask permission. The second is stiff and does not explain the club’s request. The last assumes agreement and is pushy, which is not suitable when asking a favor.

items.stem:
(1) The student council has now read every lunch survey form. (2) Students asked for larger portions, more fresh fruit, and shorter lines. (3) The council will present the results to the cafeteria manager next week. (4) The manager has agreed to review the findings.

Which sentence would be the best concluding sentence for this paragraph?
options: Fresh fruit is a healthy food that comes in many varieties.
The council also plans to survey students about school clubs, sports, and after school activities later this year.
With the manager’s help, these requests may soon lead to a better lunch experience for everyone.
Lunch is served at noon every day except Fridays.
items.explanation: The concluding sentence should bring the paragraph to a close by looking ahead from the requests and the manager’s agreement. The sentence about fruit is a general fact. The plan to survey clubs begins a new, unrelated topic. The serving time is a minor detail that does not sum up the survey results.

items.stem:
(1) The electric bus trial lasted ten weeks. (2) The bus carried about 400 riders each day. (3) The bus needed charging every night.

Which is the best way to combine sentences 2 and 3 to show a contrast?
options: The bus carried about 400 riders each day, so it needed charging every night.
The bus carried about 400 riders each day, the bus needed charging every night.
Because the bus carried about 400 riders each day, it needed charging every night.
The bus carried about 400 riders each day, yet it needed charging every night.
items.explanation: Carrying many riders and needing a nightly charge are two facts that sit in tension in this paragraph about limits, so yet states the contrast. So and because claim that the riders caused the charging, a cause and effect link that sentence 3 does not state. The comma only version is a comma splice.

items.stem:
(1) Finally, they pressed the finished books under a board for a full day. (2) The workshop teaches a simple notebook in four stages. (3) Second, they stitched the folded sheets along the spine. (4) First, each student trimmed and folded the paper. (5) Third, they glued a cloth cover over the stitched block.

Which order of sentences is the most logical for this description?
options: Sentence 4, sentence 3, sentence 5, sentence 1, sentence 2
Sentence 2, sentence 3, sentence 4, sentence 5, sentence 1
Sentence 2, sentence 4, sentence 3, sentence 5, sentence 1
Sentence 2, sentence 4, sentence 3, sentence 1, sentence 5
items.explanation: The general statement about four stages should open the paragraph, then the stages follow in the order marked by First, Second, Third, and Finally. Starting with a stage leaves the general statement at the end. Putting Second before First or Finally before Third breaks the sequence the signal words establish.

items.stem:
Composting does more than shrink the trash pile. ______ One resident said the pilot made her more aware of how much food her family threw away each week. After a month, her household cut its food waste by half.

Which detail best supports the claim that composting changes habits?
options: The bins were delivered by city workers on a Monday morning in January, before the pilot began.
Compost can be used as fertilizer in gardens and parks.
The city picked up the bins in a large truck.
Participants began planning meals more carefully so that fewer groceries went unused.
items.explanation: The claim is about changing how people behave, so the best support describes a new habit, planning meals to waste less. The delivery day and the pickup truck are logistics. The use of finished compost is true and interesting but concerns what compost is for, not how the participants changed their habits.

items.stem:
(1) The tutoring program gives students extra reading time. (2) The program also helps students gain confidence. (3) The program offers a quiet space for homework after school. (4) The program holds a small party at the end of each term.

Which revision best improves the cohesion of these sentences by reducing repetition?
options: The tutoring program gives students extra reading time. The tutoring program also helps students gain confidence. The tutoring program offers a quiet space.
The tutoring program gives students extra reading time, helps them gain confidence, offers a quiet space for homework, and ends each term with a small party.
The tutoring program gives students extra reading time, it helps them gain confidence, it offers a quiet space for homework after school and a party.
Giving extra reading time, a quiet space is offered by the tutoring program, and confidence is gained at a party each term.
items.explanation: The correct choice uses one subject with parallel verb phrases, so the details read as a list of what the program does. The first wrong choice repeats the program as the subject and drops a detail. The second is a run on with commas between clauses. The last is a tangle of passive voice and mismatched subjects.

items.stem:
Welcome, young scientists!

(1) Today you will help launch a weather balloon at the school field. (2) The balloon will carry a camera high above the clouds. (3) Atmospheric ascent is facilitated by the buoyant properties of helium gas.

This handout is for third graders. Which revision of sentence 3 best fits the purpose and audience?
options: Helium is lighter than air, so it lifts the balloon up, up, and away.
The balloon will rise because the density of the gas inside is less than the surrounding air at sea level.
Helium gas is a chemical element with two protons and two neutrons in its nucleus.
Balloons are cool, and helium is really, really neat stuff.
items.explanation: Young children need a short, clear, friendly explanation of why the balloon rises, and the correct choice gives that in plain words. The first wrong choice is accurate but too technical. The second shifts to atomic details that do not explain the lift. The last is casual but explains nothing, so it fails the purpose of the handout.
